thread:
Maya: heads-up 10 I'm drafting a smaller-scope proposal: "priority shims" for reserved customers to reduce SLA risk during cluster-wide preemptions. Idea: give a short-lived priority token that reduces preemption chance for critical sessions. Needs feasibility + launch gating.
Arjun: quick take: doable at allocator layer. Token = session-level priority boost for N seconds. Can be enforced by scoring in the allocator. Downsides: if overused, instant slots get starved. Need per-tenant rate limit + global cap.
Sienna: ops comment: any token that blocks preemption must honor drain semantics. Suggest default token_ttl=120s and drain_grace=60s. Add eviction audit log and a metric tenant.priority_tokens.used.
Noah: autoscale impacts: we should avoid permanently reserving capacity. Tokens should be soft boosts that influence scheduling, not hard slot reservations. Also add a decay factor so repeated use has diminishing returns.
Elena: CS feedback: customers will want visibility of token spend and an API to request tokens programmatically (so they can guard critical webhook flows). Also want a console counter and export.
Priya: sales note: customers will ask about billing. Two models: included tokens per month for reserved customers, or paid add-on. Finance prefers included small allotment.
Maya: proposed defaults: token_ttl=120s, default_tokens=200/month for reserved, global_instant_boost_cap=10% of cluster instant pool, decay=0.5 on repeated uses within 5m. Launch gates: allocator impl + token ledger + console counter + eviction audit.
Arjun: config sketch: 
```
priority_shim:
  enabled: true
  token_ttl_seconds: 120
  default_tokens_per_month: 200
  global_boost_cap_percent: 10
  decay_window_seconds: 300
  decay_factor: 0.5
```
Arjun: we need to ensure KV cache affinity is communicated: boosted sessions may still miss cache warmup and see higher latencies initially.
Sienna: monitoring: tenant.priority_tokens.remaining, tenant.priority_tokens.rate5m, tenant.evictions.critical.count, cluster.boost.utilization. Alert: if boost_utilization > 80% for 30m we should throttle issuance.
Noah: autoscale circuit-breaker: if allocator error_rate > 2% while boosts active, pause new boosts and shrink global_instant_boost_cap by 50%.
Elena: pilot ask: allow manual grant of extra tokens for a small number of pilot customers (customer ops flow). CS needs audit trail and notification on grants.
Priya: also include sample language for contracts: "Priority tokens reduce likelihood of preemption but do not constitute a hard SLA unless purchased as business-hours shield add-on." Keeps legal cushion.
Maya: rollout timeline: week 0 RFC -> week 1 allocator prototyping -> week 2 token ledger + API -> week 3 telemetry + console -> week 4 internal canary (2 internal tenants) -> week 6 closed pilot (1 customer with token grant). Owners: Arjun (allocator), Noah (autoscale integration), Sienna (ops/telemetry), Elena (pilot coordination), Priya (sales comms), Maya (PM).
rfc-bot: RFC posted: https://redwood.infra/rfc/priority-shims-2026 - please review by EOD Wed. :eyes:
Sienna: small nit: include rollback path: revoke all active tokens and fall back to legacy preempt policy if eviction_rate rises > threshold for 15m.
Arjun: agreed. Also add an integration test that simulates spikes and verifies decay behavior.
Maya: will update RFC with rollout gates, config, and rollback. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Priya: will draft sales one-pager and token FAQ.
Elena: will line up pilot customer and prepare onboarding checklist.
Maya: follow-up sync Friday 11am PT. End.
